operations.name: MOUNTv3 MNT
operations.placement: v3 only, separate MOUNT program100005/version3/proc1 before LOOKUP/READ
operations.effect: server creates export root filehandle; does not grant file access

operations.name: SETCLIENTID; SETCLIENTID_CONFIRM
operations.placement: v4.0 only, before OPEN; no EXCHANGE_ID/SEQUENCE/session
operations.failure: missing required state credential is local acquisition; expired READ state is NFS4ERR_EXPIRED
operations.effect: SETCLIENTID/CONFIRM installs clientid. The selected first OPEN returns OPEN4_RESULT_CONFIRM; PUTFH/OPEN_CONFIRM advances to a confirmed stateid generation before READ. No v4.1 session or SEQUENCE.

operations.name: EXCHANGE_ID; CREATE_SESSION
operations.placement: v4.1/4.2 bootstrap compounds without SEQUENCE; later session compounds have SEQUENCE first
operations.failure: returned state-protection policy not meeting client requirement is a local negotiation refusal; no invented unsupported-SP4 status
operations.effect: machine principal uses integrity/privacy; returned must_enforce/must_allow checked, user OPEN/READ not inferred from machine authority

operations.name: LOOKUP at security boundary
operations.placement: SEQUENCE,PUTFH(parent),LOOKUP(private); PUTFH followed by LOOKUP cannot return WRONGSEC
operations.failure: LOOKUP NFS4ERR_WRONGSEC; never generic READ WRONGSEC
operations.effect: A PUTFH/LOOKUP compound receives an actual LOOKUP WRONGSEC result. A distinct SEQUENCE/PUTFH/SECINFO(name) or SECINFO_NO_NAME(CURRENT_FH) query sets then consumes current FH. No-common response offers integrity service2 only; tampered unauthenticated query returns AUTH_SYS only; strict privacy service3 selection therefore finds no acceptable tuple.

operations.name: RPCSEC_GSS DATA
operations.failure: used/below-window sequence silently discarded; no server error delivered to client; altered integrity/privacy body stops before dispatch
operations.effect: header MIC covers RPC header through credential; reply MIC covers request sequence; integrity/privacy covers XDR(sequence||arguments/results)

operations.name: OPEN/READ/CLOSE
operations.placement: v4 namespace COMPOUND ends OPEN,GETFH, including SECINFO retry. OPEN returns stateid; following GETFH returns filehandle. READ uses verified GETFH handle/stateid; CLOSE sequence/stateid local result then client acceptance
operations.failure: mapping deny NFS4ERR_ACCESS; read-only WRITE NFS4ERR_ROFS; ACL deny NFS4ERR_ACCESS
operations.effect: export authorization, filesystem authorization, result generation, client accepted bytes separate

operations.name: BIND_CONN_TO_SESSION
operations.placement: v4.1 standalone COMPOUND on new connection, existing sessionid, CDFC4_FORE, no SEQUENCE; machine proof if returned must_enforce contains BIND
operations.failure: missing/wrong machine proof denies association; previous session retained
operations.effect: session retry uses new GSS sequence and same slot sequence; cache returns existing result without second side effect

operations.name: AUTH_TLS NULL probe
operations.placement: same TCP connection before ClientHello; credential flavor7 empty; verifier AUTH_NONE empty
operations.failure: only MSG_ACCEPTED and AUTH_NONE verifier octets STARTTLS accepted; accept_stat alone insufficient
operations.effect: not HTTPS or new port; strict policy never cleartext fallback

operations.name: TLS1.3 RPC transport
operations.placement: ClientHello ALPN sunrpc; server selected ALPN in encrypted EncryptedExtensions
operations.failure: certificate/name/time/trust/ALPN/client proof/revocation/host policy at independent local checks; corrupt record no decoded RPC
operations.effect: endpoint private keys stay local; each endpoint derives a master secret from its local handshake-secret HKDF state and directional application secrets from that master secret plus transcript through server Finished, before client-certificate/host-policy denials. Server alerts encrypt with tls-s2c-server; client decrypts with tls-s2c-client. Derivation grants no admission; failed connection ephemeral/HKDF/traffic keys are disposed after protected alert receipt. AUTH_SYS remains asserted per-user

operations.name: OPEN_CONFIRM
operations.placement: v4.0 only; selected first OPEN sets OPEN4_RESULT_CONFIRM; following GETFH result is verified before PUTFH(that filehandle),OPEN_CONFIRM(stateid,open-owner seqid1) before any READ; never in v4.1/4.2
operations.failure: No READ permitted before the selected confirmation requirement is satisfied
operations.effect: Server creates confirmed stateid generation2; client verifies response before installing it and releasing provisional stateid

operations.name: SEQUENCE client/server slot knowledge
operations.placement: First operation of each ordinary v4.1/4.2 compound; not EXCHANGE_ID/CREATE_SESSION/BIND bootstrap; CLOSE also consumes next slot sequence
operations.failure: Bad RPC GSS sequence/body stops before NFS SEQUENCE and leaves both accepted slot counters unchanged
operations.effect: Server advances accepted slot on valid SEQUENCE dispatch; client advances only after verifying corresponding reply. Security recovery consumes slot1 WRONGSEC, slot2 SECINFO, slot3 retry OPEN/GETFH, slot4 READ, slot5 CLOSE. Ordinary OPEN/GETFH,READ,CLOSE consumes1/2/3. NFS08 additionally consumes slot2 GETATTR(owner,owner_group), then slot3 READ and slot4 CLOSE. Lost reply leaves server2/client1; fresh-GSS retry uses same NFS slot2 and cached result.

invariants: TGT never carried to NFS; server service key never held by client
Ciphertext receipt contains no decoded fields or accepted file bytes
Integrity-only body readable untrusted at receipt, accepted only after MIC and sequence checks
Initiator subkey and acceptor subkey separate; selected per-message key acceptor subkey; server creates it, client acquires after AP-REP verification
Every operational field has instanceId, representation, sourceEventId, exactValueRef and creator/holders/inspectors
Negative stops at first detector; no deletion of cached TGT or unrelated Bob context/session
No GSSv3, delegation, labels, pNFS, COPY or optional NFS14 implementation

NFS slot0 counters include every actual session compound: ordinary OPEN/READ/CLOSE1/2/3, WRONGSEC/SECINFO/retry OPEN/READ/CLOSE1/2/3/4/5. Server dispatch and client verified-reply knowledge are separate. Cached NFS results are replaced on new slot progress, never confused with a reusable RPC/GSS envelope.

nfs.gssSequence is the focused primary READ/retry RPC sequence, not an assertion about the last bootstrap/CLOSE/DESTROY header; all those distinct exact header sequences remain authored operational fields.

Successful cleanup verifies the real server DESTROY reply before local disposal; server disposes after sending its verifier. Bob cache/context, machine session and previously accepted file bytes are not retroactively erased.

nfs.currentFilehandle is the security-query compound CURRENT_FH demonstrator, not a persistent client handle cache. Planning a subsequent PUTFH does not change a server register. The consumed-handle negative appends real GETFH to the same query compound, fails at the server, then returns successful earlier operation results and the real error.

RFC7530 16.33/16.34 and RFC8881 18.35/18.36 carry SETCLIENTID/CONFIRM or EXCHANGE_ID/CREATE_SESSION procedure arguments/results. The locally installed machine GSS context and AUTH_SYS client configuration are not those procedure arguments and must not be transported as results. RPC credential handles identify an existing context without exporting its local configuration or key.

A repeated IPC delivery of an accepted principal is a new holding acquisition occurrence of the same artifact generation. Message inbox, sender serialization and receiver-accepted copies identify their canonical source event; retaining an earlier receipt neither recreates its artifact nor turns a later message into a duplicate acquisition.

SETCLIENTID_CONFIRM returns its own status result, not a retransmitted clientid object. Confirmation and CLOSE release the exact client stateid holding installed by the corresponding verified OPEN/OPEN_CONFIRM reply, while retained protected packet captures remain history rather than active file authority.

RFC9846 record protection and RFC2203 5.3.3.2 result protection keep construction/signing of local plaintext separate from encrypting its wire representation. Exact field replay labels the latter encrypt, not a second indistinguishable derive of the same field; both occurrences retain their real canonical source event and exact representation/value.

RFC7530 3.3.2, 13.1.6.3, 13.2 and 15.2.4: NFS05/sys-refused is a server-local PUTROOTFH security-policy rejection in the namespace compound, not a client-local detector. The client cannot know that result at namespace-security or at unparsed receipt; its positive clientKnowsFailure checkpoint is namespace-security-failure-accept after the actual error response. The original true-at-server-detector predicate conflated those occurrences; the server/client split and denial outcome are retained.

BIND response protection is created locally by the server using the selected machine context; its verifier binds the request sequence and its body MIC binds the returned result. Server association precedes the reply, but client usability waits for client-local verification. A wrong-principal maintenance attempt uses the explicitly preaccepted alternate context and its own key, not the original context paired with another generation's key.

scenarios.profile: NFS-LINUX-R1: offline Linux-oriented standards illustration, revision2026-10-21. TCP; supported optional features explicitly fixed; no tested kernel/build claim. NFSv4.1/4.2 standards profile; one server, two TCP connections; SP4_MACH_CRED requires BIND_CONN_TO_SESSION in returned must_enforce bitmap; no pNFS/trunking topology expansion.
prerequisites: Accepted NFS06 session and fixed state-protection policy; same server identity verified by the profile.
Existing user GSS context and a deterministic outstanding request/slot fixture.
requiredFlow: Open a second connection and bind it using the required protected machine context.
Server checks binding conditions before associating it with the existing session; client verifies the response before marking connection usable.
Send an ordinary user request through the added connection; apply user authorization as before.
Demonstrate a lost response and permitted session replay using a fresh acceptable GSS RPC sequence with the same NFS slot request.
negativeRequirements: Possession of sessionid without required proof does not bind a connection.
Wrong principal or invalid proof fails before connection usability.
Replayed GSS sequence is rejected/discarded by GSS handling; a distinct valid session retry returns the recorded result.
One connection fails: display surviving session state only where the selected trace permits it.
acceptance: No copied SMB binding flags, SMB signing keys or automatic KDC exchange per connection.
Test no duplicate application side effect and no privilege gain.
Failed binding does not manufacture usable connection state.
Name NFS session binding, GSS/TLS channel binding and TLS session as three distinct concepts.

scenarios.profile: NFS-LINUX-R1: offline Linux-oriented standards illustration, revision2026-10-21. TCP; supported optional features explicitly fixed; no tested kernel/build claim. NFSv4.2/TCP; sec=sys; default xprtsec=mtls, named tls comparison; TLS1.3 RFC9846; TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, X25519, ECDSA P-256 certificate signatures (ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256), no resumption/0-RTT.
prerequisites: TLS helper configured, explicit trust and host authorization policy.
Visible server/client certificate identities; different endpoint private-key handles.
Apply the ALPN discrepancy disposition in the source notes before coding the wire flight.
requiredFlow: Use the RPC NULL procedure with empty AUTH_TLS credential and empty AUTH_NONE verifier. Accept only MSG_ACCEPTED with an AUTH_NONE verifier containing the eight ASCII octets STARTTLS; then start TLS on that same TCP connection. The probe accept_stat is not itself the TLS-support criterion.
Perform TLS1.3, including the server request for a client identity; tls may accept no client certificate, mtls requires the selected valid identity.
Separate certificate receipt, local handshake-key derivation/decryption, certificate/proof validation and established transport.
Carry AUTH_SYS RPC in application-data ciphertext, followed by receiver-local decoded RPC.
Show two client user IDs on the same host transport; apply export/squash/file policy independently for each.
negativeRequirements: Client certificate absent in required-mtls profile: transport not admitted.
Valid client certificate but host unauthorized: no accepted association.
Valid TLS with forged UID: no invented user-identity proof.
Corrupted application-data record: no decoded RPC or file effect.
acceptance: Only outer TLS record is visible on wire; decoded RPC appears at the receiver’s actual decrypt event.
No HTTPS wrapping or separate invented NFS-TLS port.
Each endpoint derives its own directional traffic-secret objects; private keys never move.
TLS-only and mTLS badges describe hosts; sec=sys remains client-asserted user identity.

prerequisites: A single failure input changes one condition; retain the same declared protection policy.
Certificate validation includes the chosen identity/use/time/revocation policy; offline revocation outcomes are synthetic, not live OCSP claims.
requiredFlow: Attempt the NFS11 discovery/handshake until the selected failure detector.
Record the actual failing protocol/local-policy stage and the client’s observation.
Stop the selected connection/mount attempt; keep the request undispatched and application data unavailable.
Show a concise repair hint tied to that cause; an opportunistic comparison, if displayed, is a separate explicitly labeled policy.
negativeRequirements: Unsupported/malformed AUTH_TLS reply: do not send ClientHello.
Wrong server name or untrusted/expired certificate: validation fails.
Missing/incompatible sunrpc ALPN: no accepted RPC transport.
mTLS-required client identity missing or invalid; selected revocation check rejects.
acceptance: No cleartext retry under strict policy.
No phantom GSS failure or NFS wrong-password error.
Client-side failure knowledge follows actual response/local validation; no instantaneous shared global status.
Retry/reset cannot reuse rejected transport keys as an established channel.
